text_fidelity_a:
White Mountain Puzzles "Best Sellers", Vintage Book Covers Collage, 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:78107723a2cc7136d45eaaf7dde95a97]] This was such a fun puzzle. It's probably the most enjoyable puzzle that I've ever put together. It has just the right mix of interesting text, pictures, and a variety of colors and patterns. Plus, it has tons of fun books that generate a lot of conversation as you're putting together this puzzle with friends.

I have a really small table, and so the puzzle just barely fit. You probably have a bigger table, and so you'll probably have plenty of room for this puzzle.

The quality of the puzzle was great. The pieces were nice and thick, and the pieces are pretty big for a 1000-piece puzzle. I really enjoyed this, and I'd highly recommend it to everyone that's interested in puzzles.

Pros:
+Great construction
+Excellent book cover art
+Extremely fun to put together
+Easy to medium difficulty for a 1000-piece puzzle

Cons:
-I don't think all of these are actually best sellers, even though they are all really interesting books

Here is a list of the books featured in this puzzle: Oliver Twist, The Cat in the Hat, Romeo and Juliet, Return to Peyton Place, The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, Sanctuary, To Kill a Mockingbird, Classic Fairy Tales, Moby Dick, Wild West Stories: Bare Fists, Anne of Green Gables, Gone with the Wind, Treasure Island, The Case of the Lucky Loser, A Tale of Two Cities, The Caine Mutiny, Catch-22, Animal Farm, The Joy Luck Club, Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf, Black Beauty, Stewart Little, Uncle Tom's Cabin, The Little Red Hen, The Godfather, Tarzan, War of the Worlds, The Catcher in the Rye, Jaws, Of Mice and Men, Love Story, The Tale of Peter Rabbit, The Invisible Man, The Pocket Book of Baby and Child Care, The Diary of a Young Girl: Anne Frank, The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, The Old Man and the Sea, Frankenstein, The Time Machine, Charlotte's Web, The Color Purple, The Mask of Zorro, Around the World in 80 Days, 1984, Heidi, The Hobbit, The Grapes of Wrath, The Count of Monte Cristo, The Great Gatsby, Sherlock Holmes, Black Beauty (again), The Secret Garden

text_fidelity_a: HABA Wooden 21pc Varius Building Blocks (Made in Germany) I am a sucker for beautiful, functional toys so this HABA set naturally caught my eye. These wooden blocks are precision cut and finished. They are smooth, with no sharp edges or chips. I love the bright colors. This set comes with a book of 21 different patterns to replicate. The box is made of sturdy cardstock. Both of my 6 y/o grandsons enjoyed completing different designs suggested in the book. I am happy to be able to offer them something besides typical box store toys. I do believe this set of blocks would also be great for older disabled individuals to help develop hand-eye coordination, small motor skills, etc. I think my dad would have enjoyed this when he was in the early to mid stages of Alzheimers. He seemed to enjoy figuring out how to put things together. With that in mind, I believe this would also be a fine gift for a nursing or senior living facility in memory of a loved one.

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

LEGO Hidden Side Graveyard Mystery 70420 Building Kit, App Toy for 7+ Year Old Boys and Girls, Interactive Augmented Reality Playset (335 Pieces) I hope they don't overdo it, but this new LEGO Augmented Reality system is quite cool.

There is an app that you download to your phone, and using that app, you can view your LEGO set, and watch it move and change a little bit. If you've seen someone playing Pokemon Go or using a filter on their camera phone, you'll get the idea. It works surprisingly well given that it's easy to slightly alter the design. The app itself is downloadable on iTunes and Android, and works well on the Android system, although you really likely want to use a phone because of the size of the tablet. It will work, but it gets in the way of play.

Like all parents, I'm not entirely thrilled about yet another excuse to hand over my phone, but I think that the augmented reality piece is really more of a gimmick that my daughter will tire of sooner rather than later. The building of the set must come first in order for this to work, and that's mildly educational, and we get to play with the LEGO set without the phone as well.

And did I mention how cool this set is, even without the augmented reality? The ghost theme makes for some cool pieces, and I like how this one looks when it's done. It's a winner.

It's our joy to be able to provide quality toys for our grandchildren now that we are older. This one definitely fills the bill. It is well made. I am 54 yrs. old and with a little time (4.5 - 5 hrs.) and elbow grease, I had it put together. Quite proud of myself, actually. :0) There are LOTS of pieces. But the reaction of my 3 yr. old grand daughter when she got it was priceless. Money can't buy that kind of thing. Anyhow...I'd definitely buy it again. It is just the kind of toy that sparks imagination in children and lets them be a kid.

Suggestion for whomever assembles it. Lay out all your parts & screws & count them to make sure they're all there. It would be a horrible dissappointment to get partially through and not be able to complete the project because of some missing parts. We did have one missing part, but it wasn't the worse thing. It was just the canopy over the bed, which my daughter ordered immediately and got with no problems, along with two of the roof pieces that had bent corners. This company is awesome to work with. They shipped it right away...no questions asked.

And the price was good too being it wasn't a used item. Much better than I could get at any local store.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Annabelle Wooden Dollhouse with Elevator, Balcony and 17 Accessories, Gift for Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends MINIS playset with 3 action-Packed stunt tracks! Great toy. Easy to assemble and good quality. Instructions are easy to follow. Took me about 15 mins. Does not come with batteries.

Pros:
1) easy assembly
2) holds out son’s attention span for about 30 mins
3) light weight and easy handling by toddler
4) easy storage- doesn’t take up a lot of room
5) 3 different race tracks with inter changeable track section
6) easy system to understand for a 2.5 year old

Cons (1 star deduction):
1) design flaws: if child feeds too many minis into the track it tends to creat a jam at the starting point and stop the track (easy fix: remove the minis)
2) design flaw: it also knocks off the minis if jammed
3) the interchangeably track part tends to create a jam if not lined up exactly and one has to be quick. A child might not have enough agility to be quick changing the track creating a jam if too many minis on the track.

No toy is perfect. With that said our son loves it and even we enjoy playing with it. That is all that counts and seeing the joy on his face is all this needs. It so worth purchasing this.

We use the mini as rewards system for our son’s potty training. He enjoys playing with them so much that we decided to get him the track before Christmas 🎄
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends MINIS playset with 3 action-Packed stunt tracks!

Ontel Magic Tracks The Amazing Racetrack That Can Bend, Flex and Glow - As Seen On TV Multicolor, 11' Like many people, I have seen this product advertised on television and was excited to see if it is as fun as it looks in the commercials. The set comes with 1 car, a sheet of stickers to decorate the car, and 20 track segments in four different colors. The car requires 2 AAA batteries that are NOT included. The track segments are made of small individual pieces, which is why the box says it comes with 220 pieces of track.

The track is flexible and can be arranged in many different ways, and each segment can be used as a straight or curved part of the track. The car worked well and stayed on the track. A small pamphlet with quick trips is included with ideas on making the track more fun. I used the cardboard pieces used to package the car to create a small ramp and tunnel which worked better than I expected. After the track pieces were exposed to bright light, they did slightly glow in the dark. However, the box shows a picture of a looped track. I tried both a couple types of loops and none of them worked because the flexible track wouldn't support the weight of the car. In spite of this, this is a fun racetrack set that allows for a lot of different track formations to keep kids interested.
text_fidelity_b: Ontel Magic Tracks The Amazing Racetrack That Can Bend, Flex and Glow - As Seen On TV Multicolor, 11'

Once the valve is closed, the glitter stays inside both the tube and the crown portion of the float and moves around loosely and looks cute. The float is hard to fully inflate, but even if it’s a little underinflated, it works great in the pool.

The bottom part is like an innertube and it’s comfortable for an adult to float in. There are small plastic handles on each side of the innertube, which reminds me of a raft at a water park. The “crown” part of the float doesn’t just look cute. It also provides something to lean your back and head against so you’re more comfortable in the water. I am really happy to have this float for my pool this season.

32" Play Kitchen, 2 in 1 Toy Kitchen & Grill Playset Kitchen Pretend Play Toys Kitchen Playset Kids Kitchen Set with Cooking Accessories Pros: The kids love the kitchen playset, so much so that my 4.5-year-old niece preferred it to playing her favorite computer game for a full week and the 2-year-old couldn't be tempted away even by birthday cake. It's still the first toy she heads for when she visits. One kid can play on each side, so they can play at the same time. They didn't seem bothered that things didn't work quite right. I also like that they have whole food cooking ingredients (fruit, veggies, meat, eggs) rather than a bunch of finished foods or deserts.

Cons: The kitchen is basically held together by the parts having been firmly pressed into place. Thus, even lifting it by the roof can cause parts to come off. We've moved the kitchen around several times with no problem as long as you use the handles on the purple side panels. The oven and cupboard doors were initially hard to open, but luckily use has loosened this up some. The sink faucet pulls out during play, one of the BBQ-stick holders comes off very easily (when removing the stick to put food on or off), and some of the stickers don't want to stay on. Replacing the batteries is going to be a pain as they're on the underside of the cooking surface. The plastic food is a soft plastic, so the egg got crushed when stepped on. And cooking sure is noisy! I wish there was a way to lower the volume. So the adults feel like this isn't as good a product as it could be (3 stars) but the kids give it 5 stars.

ORIGINAL: This kitchen and grill playset is the perfect height for my two-year-old niece to play with. She likes to pretend like she is cooking, so she enjoys playing with the set. There is some assembly required, and the instructions are simply line drawings. Keep the box since looking at the two sides in the pictures is of more help in assembly than the instructions. Keep in mind that you will not fully tighten the joints until done with the first couple steps. The barbecue sign is a thin sheet of cardboard, so I assume that the thicker board is supposed to be put in the slot along with it. I don't know why they didn't just print the sign on the thicker board or even just past it on. As it is, you're trying to fit two separate sheets into a slot seemingly meant only for the thicker one. I had someone try to help me get it into the slot, but it was too tight to get in very far. I ended up cutting off some of the top just to make it fit (though it turns out I didn't need to do this. It could have just stuck up without running into anything). Except for this, assembly was not particularly difficult.

You use three AA batteries to power the sound. Once you hook up the spigot, you can put water in the sink and then pump it out through the spigot. The plastic food was recognizable as specific types of food, and the pots, plates, utensils, and bottles are distinct and fairly sturdy. Since it is merely pressure that fastens the joints together, this could come apart under especially hard play, but it's unlikely a two-year-old will cause any problems with it. Overall, I'm pleased and my niece is extremely happy to play with it when visiting my house.

UPDATE: The stickers are coming off after about a week, and not just because of use. They just didn't stick well to the water bottle and utensils. The handles on the cupboard about the oven is difficult to open because there's nothing to really get a grip on the handle. It's the perfect height for a 2-year-old, but my 4.5-year-old niece has to kneel to use it. (We wanted something small since we don't have lots of room to store the toys, but this maybe isn't something that will span a large age range.)

text_fidelity_a:
Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.
text_fidelity_b: Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA

text_fidelity_a:
Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder This version adds difficulty without making it more interesting. In this game, there are both railways and ship routes to build, which means you have to collect cards for each route in the correct color and mode of transportation. Effectively, this game adds twice the number of colors you have to collect to build things. In the original game, you always end up with a bunch of cards in your hand that aren't useful to you because they're not the colors you need to finish your tickets. This game is twice as bad in that regard. Furthermore, there are fewer ship cards, even though you're expected to build more ship routes than train routes. Many of the ship cards are actually worth 2 of that color, which theoretically allows you to collect fewer cards of that color before building, but what actually happens is that you can go through the entire stack of ship cards without getting what you need because the other players are unintentionally hoarding the few cards in the color and type you need.

I didn't hate this game, but I wouldn't play it again.
text_fidelity_b: Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual My child's science project last year was growing crystals. We had lots of fun using different temperature liquids, chemicals, etc. to see which would grow fastest, best, make the most solid of crystals and even made rock candy as a "take home" treat. I love the creativity of this kit. It allows for you to create UP TO 13 different experiments (but if you cheat you can get a couple more out of it). Some of the chemicals used are not safe for young kids so I'd highly suggest sticking to the recommended manufacturer's age. Not to mention the fact that some of the crystals will take longer than a week to fully form -- most kids don't have the patience to wait. Not waiting the proper amount of time to ensure the solidity of the crystals will result in disappointment as you can imagine something that isn't solid enough can break very easy. Following directions is paramount! Make sure you sit with your child and read through all of the instructions before beginning. I'd suggest sticking with the easiest project first to get their feet wet on experimenting then gradually go through the "harder" ones. I do like that the simple purchase of extra chemicals (or using sugar) can add a lot more fun to your kit. Thames & Kosmos is a good company. They even provide online printable instructions along side the greatly illustrated manual. http://www.thamesandkosmos.com/news/manualsamples/659127_glowingcrystals_manual_sample.pdf
The price of the kit is very fair. In fact, I'd say it would be an excellent science fair project to conduct with your child this spring. Start practicing now and wow the judges with modified versions. Just be sure to do your homework. Check out books from your local library on growing crystals and start taking notes. This could be a really fun learning experience for grade-schoolers and homeschoolers alike. The only thing I thought was slightly cheesy was the "treasure case" and the shapes (thus my four stars). But kids will get a kick out of them.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual

The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games The Wolves is a quick game that looks easy to play, but it sure is not that.

The basic mechanic of the game is to manipulate your terrain tiles to perform actions, each of which can influence how fast the game accelerates, and how you manage to score points. Everything is controlled by these terrain tiles, and so you might choose a move actions specifically so that you can flip a tile that will allow you to use a Howl action. Or you may be lucky enough to flip three matches to Dominate an opponent's wolf, but that would require a lot of luck...or is it skill?

I would compare this game to 5 Tribes. None of the mechanics are similar in any way, but if you've played 5 Tribes, you might know that on your turn, you can likely identify ten different moves you could do, but it's mathematically impossible to always choose the correct action. In this game, you have a similar conundrum. What is the best move? Is it to howl at a wolf to put an extra marker on the board, or build a den that helps me establish area majority? There are turns where you legitimately have to decide between 5 different, equally powerful moves you can make, and then live with those consequences.

I do have one problem with the game, though, and that is that there are a lot of little rules to remember. Two pieces per space, you cannot be moved if you share a spot with a den, you have to re-move if someone "pushes" your pack wolves with an alpha, and alphas are the only ones who can howl. Dens can be upgraded to lairs if your den is next to water, but some spaces have rivers on them that look like water sources, but they aren't. Also, alphas have to be on the space to build a den, but can be adjacent to upgrade it. You get a reference card for some of this, and some is on the board, but it can be tricky to remember all of the specific placement rules for each different action.

This game is a lot thinkier than you might expect, and so it won't be for everyone. Everyone will want to play it though - the production quality of the game, from the art to the unique wolf meeples, is really quite excellent, and the game is rife with possibilities for expansions. The box insert is well-designed, and the maps are modular, which is great for replayability. Overall, our heavy gaming family liked our two plays of the game, and will come back to it often, because not too many games of this depth can be played this quickly.
text_fidelity_b: The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games

text_fidelity_a:
Prime Climb Great game for helping kids understand factors and learn their multiplication/division (and addition/subtraction) facts, plus it's FUN! The part that initially drew me in for where my kids are was the color coding of the basic primes, and by extension the use of those colors to represent factors in the products. Then, it arrived and the gameplay was really fun--there are two ten sided dice and you can add, subtract, multiply or divide the number you are on by each die in turn to move. If you land on a prime you get to draw a Prime Card, which you can either use right away or save for later to benefit yourself or target an opponent, depending on whether the card is an Action card or Keeper. The first person to move both pawns to 101 wins. If you get tired of the standard rules, though, they apparently have some variations here: [...] but I have not yet tried any--looking forward to doing so after we've played through a few more times.

Oh and keep in mind that it takes longer the more players there are--folks with younger kids might want to keep it to 2 or 3 players so it doesn't go so long, or modify the rules so people don't get sent back to start so often. I'm sure there are cooperative ways to play too if that's more up someone's alley, like it was for us when the kids were younger.
text_fidelity_b: Prime Climb

text_fidelity_a: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32" Purchased one of these without exactly knowing what I was buying. Sure, I knew it made noise - but didn't know how it did that or what it might sound like ( guess I could have looked on YouTube, but I didn't). Anyway, now that I've got one it's all everyone wants to play with. Basically it's a short tube with a thin piece of taut plastic covering one end (think tiny drum head), and a long loose spring mounted to the center of the plastic. Holding the tube and shaking it causes the spring to vibrate like springs do, those vibrations travel up to the drum head and the sound reverberates into the tube and is amplified out the other end. Makes for some pretty interesting sound effects. Overall I'm more than happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32"

text_fidelity_a:
Pandemic on the Brink Board Game EXPANSION | Family /Strategy /Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ |2 to 5 players | Average Playtime 45 minutes | Made by Z-Man Games , Red Pandemic has become a favorite on game nights in my circle of friends, and the On the Brink Expansion improves the experience in several ways. There are new game modes, new roles, new events, and all of them work well. On the most basic level, the ability to have five players is a big improvement. You have to relearn the board setup some to compensate for how many new events are included to keep from unbalancing the game, but none of the changes are so drastic as to be overwhelming.

Aside from this, most of the new material boils down to making the game more difficult. The most basic form of this is the addition of an additional Epidemic card to enable "Legendary" difficulty (I think we lost in ten minutes the first time we tried that mode). The Virulent Strain variation to the rules increases the power of one of the diseases. The Mutation variation adds a fifth disease. All of these are good for the increased challenge, but don't really change the core gameplay too much.

The one exceptionally different mode is the Bio-Terrorist variation, which makes one player an enemy to the rest of the group. I, like many of the other reviewers, love this mode. My friends and roommates don't all agree. It is the type of game mode that certainly has the potential to ruin friendships if you play it too often, but I think it injects some welcome variety into the game. That said, it's totally optional and the expansion has plenty of other improvements to justify buying it even if this game mode doesn't prove to be a hit with your crowd.

As a last, wonderful feature, the game box comes packaged with a tray that is capable of holding the materials not only for the expansion, but for the original game as well. This way you can actually store the original game and the expansion in a single box. It sounds like a small thing, but little touches and details like that are what separate the good game publishers from the great.
text_fidelity_b: Pandemic on the Brink Board Game EXPANSION | Family /Strategy /Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ |2 to 5 players | Average Playtime 45 minutes | Made by Z-Man Games , Red

Radio Flyer Air Ride Balance Bike, Toddler Bike, Ages 1.5-5 Pink , White It is assembled easily as mine seemed to come partially assembled beyond the scope of the directions.

It looks good, has a smooth ride, with a snazzy traditional bell to alert the neighbors.That's all good, but it needs more work at the design level.

The handlebars don't seem to attach securely, but not unsafely. A 3 year-old might not be able to loosen them, but any adult certainly can. Tighten them as hard as you can.

The cover for the handlebars -- where it attaches to the headset (just above the wheel) pops off whenever the wheel is turned. It is intended to, and does, snap in when still, but should remain snapped in always.

The bike is designed, per the packaging, for 2.5-5 year-olds. My boy turns 3 in three weeks and is considered average height. He's slightly too small. Instead, the age guidelines should describe height, not age, or both. He'll grow into it so I'm not concerned.

Overall, I'll keep it, but if I were to buy a new one, I'd buy one fully assembled, maybe even used, to ensure everything was solidly connected.

Anthony Trendl
TreeFortBooks.com
